title: Kestrel Labs - Discovery: Migration OpenAI -> Dedicated
summary: Kestrel Labs currently uses OpenAI for prod generation but is hitting cost and latency variability at scale. They are evaluating Redwood Dedicated (and Private/VPC) for predictable throughput, on-prem options for data sensitivity, and need assurance on eval parity vs OpenAI and compatibility with vLLM/TGI runtime. Agreed to run a benchmark with Kestrel prompt set; SE-led deep dive and security pack to follow.
next_steps: Redwood to send security docs (SOC2, ISO, KMS/HSM notes) - Alex
SE to run benchmark on Redwood Dedicated using Kestrel prompt set - Priya
Schedule technical deep dive on model parity and TGI/vLLM integration next week - Alex/Priya
Send draft pricing and capacity options for Dedicated (monthly commit tiers) - Alex
action_items: Alex: Share security pack + SOC2 summary by 2026-03-06
Priya: Kick off benchmarking run and share results within 7 days
Rina: Share canonical prompt set + sample evaluation metrics by EOD 2026-03-05
Ethan: Provide list of required compliance controls (KMS, audit log retention) by 2026-03-08
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex, AE at Redwood, and with me is Priya our SE. How's everyone this afternoon?
[00:07] Mark Dawson: Hey Alex, good thanks. We got a handful from Kestrel on the line; we're interested in, uh, talking through options to move off Open A I for some of our high-volume generation.
[00:18] Priya Patel: Great, thanks Mark. Quick intro from our side — Priya, SE — I focus on performance and benchmarks. Curious: can you share current usage patterns and pain points?
[00:27] Rina Gupta: Sure. We run about 6M tokens/day across customer-facing assist flows, plus nightly batch jobs for summaries. Primary issue is cost — per-token spend is high — and second is latency variability. During peak hours our p50 is okay but p95 spikes to 800-1,200ms which breaks our UX.
[00:44] Alex Chen: Totally. Are you seeing rate limit throttles from OpenAI or just latency?
[00:49] Tom (SRE): A bit of both. We've bumped into occasional 429s, and sometimes request queueing at our proxy. We also want better control — like reserved capacity — so we can guarantee throughput.
[00:59] Priya Patel: Makes sense. Sounds like a classic fit for Dedicated: reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput, plus optional Private/VPC for data-sensitive workloads. Rina — any requirements around data residency or key management?
[01:10] Rina Gupta: We have European customers and some regulated accounts that require data to stay in-region. And we want customer-managed keys, HSM/KMS integration is a hard ask for security.
[01:19] Ethan Morales: Also we need full audit logs and SSO (SAML) integration. SOC 2 is baseline — we need to see evidence.
[01:26] Alex Chen: Understood. We'll send our security pack with SOC 2, ISO notes, KMS options, and audit log retention. Redwood Dedicated supports KMS/HSM integrations and Private deployments with customer-managed networking.
[01:38] Mark Dawson: Cool. One other thing: compatibility — we use a mix of models via OpenAI endpoints, and we also run some local inference on TGI and vLLM stacks for internal experiments. How compatible is Redwood with those runtimes? Will we get parity in outputs?
[01:50] Priya Patel: Great question. Two parts: model compatibility and eval parity. Redwood's serving runtime can host a range of open weights and the platform includes model variants verified by Redwood. For parity vs OpenAI proprietary models, it depends on the weights — e.g., if you use GPT-4-like proprietary models on OpenAI, we can't replicate that unless you have exported weights. But for open models and for TGI/vLLM-compatible weights, Redwood supports those runtimes and our kernel selection and quantization profiles are tuned to preserve accuracy.
[02:16] Naomi Li: So if we move to a local open model on Redwood Dedicated, will our prompt hallucination/regression rates be similar? We run a suite of evals nightly.
[02:25] Priya Patel: We recommend running controlled evals — Redwood Optimize can help with model/quantization recommendations. We'll run your prompt set side-by-side: current OpenAI baseline vs candidate model on Dedicated. Our goal is parity in metrics you care about — F1/ROUGE/Task accuracy — and we'll surface differences.
[02:40] Mark Dawson: Sounds good. Benchmarks — what do you need from us?
[02:44] Priya Patel: A canonical prompt set, expected metrics (p95 latency target, acceptable quality delta), and a sample of typical request sizes (seq length distribution). Rina, you mentioned nightly batch jobs; can you share sequence length stats for those?
[02:55] Rina Gupta: Batch jobs are long — average 1.2k tokens, peak 4k for some documents. Interactive flows are shorter, 80–250 tokens.
[03:03] Priya Patel: Ok that's useful; long sequences change kernel selection and memory footprint. Redwood's runtime does prefix/KV caching and supports continuous batching to improve throughput on heavy workloads but we'll need to size GPU pools for the mix you described.
[03:17] Mark Dawson: What's the rough sizing model? Like how many A100-ish GPUs for our 6M tokens/day?
[03:22] Sam Ruiz: Very ballpark — depends on model and quantization. For a 13B open model in int8 noise we might fit X qps per A100; for a 70B you'd need more. We'll propose a capacity plan after we see your prompt set and seq distributions, and propose burst capacity.
[03:36] Tom (SRE): We also have an internal runtime built on v L LM for some microservices. Is Redwood able to route to our existing vllm fleet or do we need to rehost?
[03:45] Priya Patel: You can operate hybrid: use Redwood Hosted/Dedicated as primary and route to on-prem vLLM for certain routes, but that requires compatibility layer and model variant mapping. For full management in Redwood Dedicated we'd rehost the model weights on Redwood hardware. We support TGI/LangChain-like interfaces and have an API compatibility layer to reduce code changes.
[04:01] Ethan Morales: Any concerns about model weights — licensing or export — when we rehost?
[04:05] Priya Patel: You need to ensure license permits hosting. We'll help with model onboarding and vetting. For closed weights you need the vendor permission or to use vendor-hosted endpoints.
[04:13] Mark Dawson: From a cost perspective, can you give a sense of committed pricing vs pay-as-you-go?
[04:18] Alex Chen: Dedicated is committed capacity with monthly or annual tiers — typically lower per-token unit economics vs Hosted API at scale. We'll send a draft pricing spreadsheet: baseline commit, burst pool, overage rates.
[04:26] Naomi Li: Regarding eval parity, odd tokenization differences sometimes cause metric drift — do you capture tokenization variant differences?
[04:33] Priya Patel: Yes we log tokenization, and in our eval harness we can normalize by tokenizer or run with the same tokenizer as your baseline. We'll produce a side-by-side artifact.
[04:42] Mark Dawson: Security again — can Redwood Dedicated be deployed into our VPC or on-prem?
[04:46] Alex Chen: Yes. We offer Private deployments with a customer-controlled control plane and VPC peering, and there's an on-prem package for fully air-gapped needs. Many enterprise customers pick Private when they have stringent data residency or network constraints.
[04:57] Tom (SRE): For the VPC option, how does networking look — NAT, egress, and monitoring?
[05:03] Priya Patel: We support VPC peering, private endpoints, and customer-managed routing. Egress policies are configurable and audit logs can be pushed to your SIEM. We'll include network diagrams in the pack.
[05:12] Rina Gupta: One more thing: model updates and rollouts — we need canaries and fast rollback.
[05:17] Sam Ruiz: Redwood Console supports canary rollouts, A/B tests, and automatic fallbacks to another model variant if quality drops. You can pin model versions per route.
[05:26] Mark Dawson: Great. Any known gotchas migrating from Anthropic or Azure model endpoints?
[05:31] Priya Patel: Mostly around API semantics and tokenization differences. Anthropic responses sometimes include different system message behaviors; for Azure-managed models there can be subtle behavioral differences. We'll capture those in evals. For runtime, if you already run vLLM/TGI locally, we've found rehosting is straightforward for open weights but additional tuning may be required for quantization.
[05:49] Naomi Li: Timelines — how long to run a POC/bench?
[05:52] Priya Patel: Once we have your prompt set and access patterns, the initial benchmarking run can be done in about 3–7 days to collect latency and quality metrics. A POC with a small dedicated pool and integration tests can be 2–4 weeks depending on procurement.
[06:03] Alex Chen: Sounds like next steps: Rina sends prompt set and metrics; Priya will run a bench; Alex will send security docs and pricing. We'll schedule a technical deep dive next week focused on vLLM/TGI and kernel tuning.
[06:15] Mark Dawson: Yep that works. A couple of quick Qs — do you support customer-managed KMS with HSM? And what's your SLA on p95 latency for Dedicated?
[06:24] Alex Chen: Yes on KMS/HSM options. SLA depends on ring/tier but Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we'll surface the exact numbers in the proposal.
[06:33] Ethan Morales: Do you keep request logs or redact payloads?
[06:36] Priya Patel: Logs can be configured. By default we store metadata and traces; payload retention is configurable and can be disabled for sensitive routes. We'll include options in security pack.
[06:47] Naomi Li: Any existing customers who've migrated from OpenAI with similar scale?
[06:50] Alex Chen: Yes, a few references — we'll include anonymized case studies and a reference list.
[06:55] Mark Dawson: Perfect. If you can get the security docs and the benchmark plan this week that would be ideal.
[06:59] Alex Chen: Will do. Thanks everyone for your time. Looking forward to the POC.
[07:04] Rina Gupta: Thanks — talk soon.
notes: Occasional transcription artifacts: 'v L LM' for vLLM, 'KV cash' used once. AE+SE pairing observed. Customer emphasized SOC2, KMS/HSM, VPC, and eval parity. Action items captured above.
